justification: Ἀπόλλων (Euthd. 302d, Smp. 197a): the lowercase key reads only as a Homeric/Ionic imperfect of ἀπολάω, so the god was filed under a lemma 'ἀπό-λάω' with no entry.
Σωκράτης: the lowercase key reads it as σωκρατέω 'Socratize' (Ar. Av. 1282), so all of Socrates was filed under that verb; Plato never uses it.
Σωκράτη, accusative of Σωκράτης; see swkra/ths.
Σωκράτει, dative of Σωκράτης; see swkra/ths.
Ἀχαιῶν 'of the Achaeans' (Lg. 682e, 706d; R. 393d): the lowercase key reads only as ἀχαιά 'grief'.
ἀφιῇ (Lg. 869a, 869e; R. 520a), present subjunctive of ἀφίημι; the table reads this accentuation only as a future of ἀφίζω 'rise from one's seat'.
ἄναντες, neuter of ἀνάντης 'uphill' (Phd. 112e, Phdr. 247b, R. 568d); the table reads it only as an imperfect of a compound 'ἀνά-ἄντομαι'.
σύνηθες, neuter of συνήθης 'accustomed' (Lg. 739a, Plt. 297d, Ti. 21b); the table reads it only as a verb 'sift'. The gloss is the table's own for συνήθης, which the LSJ repair extends.
συνήθων, genitive plural of συνήθης (Lg. 799c); the table reads it only as a participle of a verb 'sift'.
